observations: body L1-L4: the upper right corner of the leaf is lost in the master scan: the scan is blank there, along a line that runs from x 451 pt at the rule under the running head (whose page number 275 is lost with it) to x 459 pt at L4, and the ends of L1-L4, 35 to 42 pt of print each (about eight letters), are lost. The visible text is transcribed and a light grey bar marks each lost end, its length that of the lost print at the scale of the edition; nothing is supplied. After «paulo» (L1) only the left side of a round letter of x-height is left at the edge (x 452.1-453.5 pt). The sense asks for «dimidium» there (7/24 of 2° is 35′, a little more than half a degree, and L2 goes on «et saepe ne dimidium quidem attingunt»), and for «provenit error» and «luminarium» at the ends of L3 and L4; the lost end of L2 opened the parenthesis that «ab)» closes in L3. The master scan is the Internet Archive file of the three parts (the same bytes); no second copy of Part I has been found to supply the lost ends.

body L5, L7-L8, L18-L20, L33-L35: heavy brackets close Schiaparelli's addition begun on p. 274, L24 (L5) and open and close those of a) (L8, L18) and b) (L20, L33); the addition of c), begun in L35, goes on to p. 276. The dashes after «a)», «b)» and «c)» measure 10.1, 9.2 and 9.6 pt, those of «39—pag.» and «22—pag.» 9.7 and 9.2 pt, those before «Schiaparelli» (L18, L33) 10.1 and 10.2 pt; «al–Battānī» (L8) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L8-L16: the first figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the shadow about O (radius 52.9 pt), its outline printed with two gaps, at the upper right and on the right, which are kept; the Moon at a, b and c (radius 16.4 pt), a and c touching the shadow inside, within 0.6 pt; the path of the Moon, solid from a to c and dashed beyond, dash by dash; the line from A through K and b to O, with the dot at O; the italic letters. AK = 12.6 pt, the radius of the shadow less Ob and the radius of the Moon; ab and bc measure 26.8 and 26.9 pt, so bc is half the path ca.

body L10, L12, L16-L17: the t's of «totalitatis» (L10), of «talis» (L12) and the second t of «totam» (L16) print without their crossbars, like an l; the m of «minuta» (L11) and of «moram» (L17) prints broken, like ın. A speck below the line before «98» (L10), 1.2 by 2.6 pt, is not a comma.

body L22-L30: the second figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the shadow of the Earth, whose printed outline is not a circle (its radius from O grows from about 86 pt on the left to 91 pt on the right), drawn along its traced centre line; the ecliptic EOA and the perpendicular through O; the Moon about D (radius 23.5 pt) and about B (radius 24.2 pt), touching the shadow inside at G and F; the lines GDO and FBO; DC and HB parallel to the ecliptic, DE and BA perpendicular to it; the line DIB; the bold italic letters; «umbra Terrae» along the left of the outline and «ecliptica» along the ecliptic, in italic. OB = OD is the radius of the shadow less that of the Moon, half the difference of the diameters; HB = OA, since OHBA is a rectangle; IB² = HB² + IH², the path from the middle of the eclipse to the end of totality.
body L28-L31: the bars over «OE» and «HB» (L28) reach over the exponents; the 2 after «HB» under the radical (L31) prints broken, only its upper hook and a speck.

notes_left L1-L2: the numerator 1 of L1 prints with a heavy flag, 3.4 pt wide, and a speck before it. Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXI) note at p. 96, l. 6 that «gradus» is to be read for «horae», referring to this note.
